notes: Builds an open-addressed (linear-probing) int->index hash table sized to the next power of two >= 1.5x the input size (`is.size + (is.size shr 1)`), a standard 2/3 load-factor calc. Backing store `anIntArray3961` is a flat array of (key, originalIndex) pairs at [2*slot]/[2*slot+1], initialized to -1 (empty). For each input value it linearly probes (mask = tableSize-1) until an empty slot, then stores the key and its original position in `is`. This matches the class-level doc note in docs/class_rename_suggestions.csv ('Instance open-addressed int hash set sized to power-of-two') and pairs with method2365 which performs the lookup half of the same scheme.

Looks up `i_37_` (the real key) in the open-addressed table built by the constructor and returns the stored original index, or -1 if absent — classic linear-probe lookup mirroring the constructor's insert logic (same mask-and-probe sequence). The first parameter `i` is never read inside the method body (only `anInt3960++` happens regardless) — it's a decoy/opaque parameter. Confirmed via Js5Archive.kt call sites, e.g. `aIntHashSet_3723!!.method2365(1, method2108(string, -29286))` where the second arg is clearly a computed name-hash (method2108 looks like a string-hash function) and the first arg is always a small constant (1, or `i xor 0x7486.inv()` / `i xor 0x1c1a` decoy-XOR patterns) — i.e. real usage always keys off the second parameter, and the caller uses the returned index to index into a parallel array (`aIntHashSetArray3728!![i_2_]`), confirming this is an index lookup keyed by hash.
